record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Generalize the notion of transversality from Volterra quadratic stochastic operators to arbitrary quadratic stochastic operators V(x) with heredity coefficients P_{ij,k}. In particular, define what it should mean for a non-Volterra or arbitrary QSO to be transversal, and then find necessary and sufficient conditions on the cubic heredity matrix P = (P_{ij,k}) that exactly characterize when the operator is transversal.

evidence.quote: A skew-symmetric matrix A is called transversal if all even order leading (principal) minors are nonzero. A Volterra QSO V is called transversal if the corresponding skew-symmetric matrix A is transversal [14],[18],[36].
Problem 2. Define concept of transversality for arbitrary QSO and find necessary and sufficient condition on matrix P = (Pij,k ) of a QSO under which the QSO is a transversal.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) on the (m-1)-dimensional simplex
S^{m-1} = { x = (x_1,...,x_m) ∈ R^m : x_i ≥ 0, Σ x_i = 1 }
is a map V : S^{m-1} → S^{m-1} of the form
(V(x))_k = Σ_{i,j=1}^{m} P_{ij,k} x_i x_j,  k = 1,...,m,
where the heredity coefficients P_{ij,k} satisfy P_{ij,k} = P_{ji,k} ≥ 0 and Σ_{k=1}^{m} P_{ij,k} = 1 for every i,j.

A QSO V is called Volterra if P_{ij,k} = 0 whenever k ∉ {i,j}. For a Volterra QSO, writing (V(x))_k = x_k(1 + Σ_{i=1}^{m} a_{ki} x_i), one obtains a skew-symmetric matrix A = (a_{ki}) with a_{ki} = 2 P_{ki,k} - 1 (so that a_{ki} = -a_{ik} and |a_{ki}| ≤ 1). A skew-symmetric matrix A is called transversal if all its leading principal minors of even order are nonzero, and a Volterra QSO is called transversal when its associated skew-symmetric matrix A is transversal.

Problem. Extend the notion of transversality from Volterra QSO to the class of all (in particular non-Volterra) quadratic stochastic operators: propose a definition of "transversal QSO" applicable to an arbitrary cubic heredity tensor P = (P_{ij,k}) that reduces to the Volterra notion above in the Volterra case, and find necessary and sufficient conditions on P that exactly characterize when the corresponding QSO is transversal in the sense of this definition.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any work that defines transversality for arbitrary (non-Volterra) quadratic stochastic operators or that characterizes such operators in terms of the heredity tensor P_{ij,k}. Surveys and recent papers on QSOs (including superpositions of Volterra and permuted Volterra operators, and non-Volterra families) discuss dynamics and fixed/periodic points but do not appear to address this specific extension of transversality. The status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators and Their Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys quadratic stochastic operators including Volterra and non-Volterra classes, without proposing a notion of transversality for general QSOs.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys on QSO dynamics do not give a transversality criterion for non-Volterra QSOs.

status_evidence.title: On a Superposition of Volterra and Permuted Volterra Quadratic Stochastic Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies superpositions of Volterra and permuted Volterra QSOs and their trajectories on the 2-simplex.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on non-Volterra-type QSOs focuses on dynamics rather than defining transversality via P_{ij,k}.
